title: refactor(usage): remove legacy session locators
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Usage lookup could let a historical `sessionEntry.sessionFile` override an explicitly selected artifact. Removing that cast alone would leave a second compatibility reader in path derivation. Both readers now disappear: usage consumes an explicit artifact or a complete canonical session target.

Canonical target validation and Gateway target selection use the existing worker read owners. The final worker entry and selected source are returned together, so visibility checks do not reuse an older snapshot after validation yields. The selected physical store is carried forward, stale key/session pairs are rejected, read failures remain failures, and captured cancellation is checked across the new awaits. A retained transcript may still outlive its metadata row. Existing JSONL/archive artifacts remain readable; malformed partial targets no longer borrow missing fields from another locator. Status cost reads select their canonical SQLite owner through the existing physical-store resolver.

This is derived usage projection cleanup. It does not rewrite or delete persisted state and needs no migration. Updates continue using canonical session targets and explicit retained artifacts; obsolete metadata no longer redirects usage reads.

Production (`src/**` and `extensions/**`, excluding tests/support): **+131/-146/net -15**. Seven production files changed; no new generic API or database schema.

Overlap: draft #161513 narrows assertions in the same resolver; #157922 changes transcript discovery/event-time behavior in the same file. This change preserves those discovery paths and will rebase if needed.

## Evidence

Final head: `32d259b99c057881d465a56459e66d4a94ea5e82`. [Exact-head normal CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36969576866) passed, including changed tests, production/test types, lint, baseline ratchets, build, and security checks. Independent Codex reviews through P2 are clean, including the fixture correction and final suppression cleanup. `oxfmt` and `git diff --check` passed.

After repeated Testbox admission failures without a runner, the coordinator-authorized [hosted fallback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36968487901) passed both attributable negative controls and all 69 tests in six focused suites. That job's independent Npm update cell failed; the Usage step and its uploaded `usage/summary.json` passed. No local tests or builds ran and this fallback uses no persistent lease.

Behavior proof is pinned to `3a99184788fe3afd11f40ed75d909773f8c5fa11`. The final head only removes an obsolete lint-suppression comment and its grandfathered baseline entry; executable behavior and tests are identical. Negative controls fail at the intended assertions: the original reader overrides an explicit artifact, and the pre-fence implementation reaches the summary loader after usage-context revocation.

Each focused command was `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` on the GitHub-hosted runner:

| File | Passed | Wall seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts` | 25 | 45.89 |
| `src/infra/session-cost-usage.archive-identity.test.ts` | 10 | 61.93 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/usage.sessions-usage.test.ts` | 10 | 41.02 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/usage.sessions-usage-context-lifecycle.integration.test.ts` | 3 | 51.22 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/usage.sessions-usage-owner-attribution.integration.test.ts` | 9 | 60.68 |
| `src/status/status-text.test.ts` | 12 | 48.41 |

The complete hosted Usage step took 507 seconds, including three frozen installs and both controls. The controls took 36.46s and 47.41s. These are full command/CI costs, not isolated assertion durations.

The first CI run caught a deterministic fixture mismatch: the combined-store mock supplied family IDs omitted by the authoritative read mock. Both now use the same typed entry; all rollup assertions remain. The canonical-source case moved into the existing archive-identity suite and gained a real-worker lineage assertion. This introduced no extra test process, sleep, timeout increase, or weaker assertion. The exact assertion baseline shrank from three to two; a subsequent obsolete max-lines suppression and its baseline entry were removed.

Existing JSONL/archive artifacts remain readable, including rowless retained transcripts. The unrelated combined-store/context and transcript readers retain their existing execution owners; this PR does not claim all usage processing is free of synchronous SQLite. The lifecycle regression protects revocation before the final target read, not every pre-existing authorization window.
